# CherryML rate matrices (external baseline)

Published rate matrices from CherryML (Prillo, Deng, Sabin, Ralph, Reddy, Song,
*CherryML: scalable maximum likelihood estimation of phylogenetic models*, Nature
Methods 2023), used here as an external baseline in the paper-2b pair-substitution
evaluation.

## Files

- `rate_matrices/Q2.txt` — the 400×400 **co-evolution** rate matrix Q2 (residue–
  residue coevolution at contacting sites). Pair states are ordered with the
  single-AA alphabet `ARNDCQEGHILKMFPSTWYV` (LG order); row/column headers give
  the two-letter pair labels.
- `rate_matrices/lg.txt` — the classical 20×20 LG matrix (same order), for format
  reference.
- `Q2_ours.npz` — Q2 remapped to our tensor pair order `ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY`
  (generated by `experiments/eval_cherryml_matrix.py`).

## Source

Zenodo record **7830072**, file `rate_matrices.tgz`:
`https://zenodo.org/records/7830072` (repo: https://github.com/songlab-cal/CherryML).

## Evaluation

`experiments/eval_cherryml_matrix.py` remaps Q2 to our alphabet, grants it its one
natural free parameter (a global rate scale, ML-fit on the training shards, since
its time axis need not match our LG-ML τ), and scores held-out per-count
transition log-likelihood on our corpora with the same metric as
`experiments/fit_pair_models.py`. Result: `results/pair_models/cherryml_q2_eval.json`.

Caveat: Q2 was trained on the trRosetta families (different cherry extraction), so
its trRosetta held-out is near-in-sample; **af_full** (deep Pfam, disjoint
alignments) is the cleaner external test — where our fitted Synchronized/Coupled
models beat it.
